From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: 
Date: 2027-02-14T17:12:00Z
Subject: Aurora Tech — capability review & proposed test matrix

Kevin — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and a proposed set of tests so we can validate where Redwood sits relative to the hyperscalers and your internal requirements. I captured notes from Sara's list of priorities and what you demoed: 

Top Aurora priorities from the call:
- Reliable function/tool-calling with schema enforcement (rides on top of external API calls)
- Deterministic structured outputs for invoice ingestion (JSON schema validation, strict field types)
- Streaming for long-form outputs with stable first-byte and mid-stream recovery
- Cost predictability: unit token costs + autoscaling limits
- Security/compliance: SSO, audit logs, and data retention control

What Aurora already tested (as discussed):
- Prototype with GCP Vertex and a Bedrock PoC. Observations were higher tail latency on streaming and inconsistent results on function-calling schema enforcement.

Where Redwood differentiates (summary):
- Streaming-first SDK with chunked first-byte guarantees and per-request fallback policies
- KV-prefix caching and request-level dedup to reduce per-token spend for repeated prompts
- Integrated function-calling with strict JSON schema validation and post-generation verifier hooks
- Dedicated pools for deterministic throughput and a documented latency SLO for short-turn responses

Proposed validation tests (we recommend running these side-by-side against your Bedrock/Vertex PoCs):
1) Function-call correctness (owner: Redwood Eng — rishi). 50 canonical tool-call cases with schema checks, edge cases (missing fields, invalid args), and 0/1/2 concurrent calls returned per generation. Success criteria: 95% schema conformance, <200ms extra latency for synchronous tool calls.
2) Structured-output compliance (owner: Aurora data team + Redwood SE). Run 1k invoice documents through prompt+schema enforcement to validate field-level types and post-parse error rates. Goal: <3% manual correction.
3) Streaming stability (owner: Redwood infra — aditya). 200 concurrent streaming sessions, variable token rates (200–2k tokens). Measure first-byte latency, reconnect behavior, and tail drops vs. Bedrock baseline.
4) Cost/throughput probe (owner: Aurora infra). Compare token cost per 1M tokens under typical prompting patterns, including prefix-caching scenarios.

Logistics / timeline suggestions:
- Technical kickoff (deep-dive): week of Feb 22. Please confirm a 90-minute slot.
- Test execution window: Feb 24–26 (3 days of runs).
- Demo of results + mutual action plan: Mar 1.

I attached a draft mutual action plan (Aurora-MAP-20270214.xlsx) that enumerates owners, test definitions, and pass/fail criteria. Next steps for you: confirm attendees for the technical kickoff and whether you want Redwood to spin a short-lived dedicated pool for the streaming run or run everything against your Bedrock/Vertex PoC for apples-to-apples comparison.

Thanks — happy to iterate this plan. I’ll loop Rishi and Aditya to own the test definitions on our side.

—
Marissa Cole
